heading: Administrative filings; timing
body_text:
170 IAC 1-6-3 Administrative filings; timing

(a) A filing described in this rule is an administrative filing, and is effective thirty (30) days after the utility submits it to the commission unless the commission, by order, suspends the filing, sets it for hearing, or rejects it.

(b) A utility shall serve a copy of each administrative filing on the office of utility consumer counselor on the same day it is submitted to the commission.

(c) A utility shall not place an administrative filing into effect before the thirty (30) day period ends, except upon written approval of the commission secretary.

(Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission; 170 IAC 1-6-3; filed Mar 3, 2008, 3:20 p.m.: 31 IR 1722)

heading: Administrative filings; contents
body_text:
(a) Each administrative filing must include a verification, a statement of the relief requested, and the supporting schedules identified in the commission's filing checklist.

(b) A filing that is incomplete may be returned by the commission secretary within ten (10) days after submission, in which case the thirty (30) day period under section 3 of this rule does not begin.

(c) A utility shall retain the workpapers supporting the filing for a period of five (5) years after the filing becomes effective.

(Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission; 170 IAC 1-6-4; filed Mar 3, 2008, 3:20 p.m.: 31 IR 1722; readopted filed Dec 12, 2024, 2:05 p.m.: 20241218-IR-170240455RFA)

heading: Administrative filings; notice
body_text:
(a) A utility shall give notice of an administrative filing by publication on its website and by posting in each business office for the period stated in section 3 of this rule.

(b) The notice must identify the filing, the effective date, and the manner in which a customer may submit comments to the commission, and must refer to "170 IAC 1-6-2(11)" for the definitions used in the notice.

(c) A utility shall file proof of notice with the commission within seven (7) days after the notice is first posted.

(Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission; 170 IAC 1-6-5; filed Mar 3, 2008, 3:20 p.m.: 31 IR 1722)

heading: Customer deposits; interest; refund
body_text:
170 IAC 4-1-13 Customer deposits; interest; refund

(a) A utility may require a deposit from a residential customer only to secure payment of bills for service, and only where the customer has an unsatisfactory credit history as determined under the utility's approved tariff.

(b) The deposit shall not exceed one-sixth (1/6) of the estimated annual billing for the customer. The utility shall give the customer a written receipt that states the amount, the interest rate, and the conditions of refund.

(c) Interest on the deposit shall accrue at the rate set by the commission from the date of deposit and shall be credited annually or paid at refund.

(d) The utility shall refund the deposit, with accrued interest, after twelve (12) consecutive months of prompt payment, or upon termination of service after deduction of any unpaid final bill.

(Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission; 170 IAC 4-1-13; filed Mar 3, 2008, 3:20 p.m.: 31 IR 1722; readopted filed Dec 12, 2024, 2:05 p.m.: 20241218-IR-170240455RFA)

heading: Disconnection; prohibited disconnections; reconnection
body_text:
170 IAC 4-1-16 Disconnection of service; prohibited disconnections; reconnection

(a) A customer may request that service be discontinued on any date after giving the utility reasonable notice. The customer remains liable for service furnished until three (3) working days after the requested discontinuance date, or until the date the utility actually discontinues service, whichever is earlier.

(b) A utility may discontinue service without prior notice when a condition on the customer's premises is dangerous or hazardous to life, physical safety, or property, or when the utility has reasonable evidence of fraudulent or unauthorized use of electricity or of tampering with the utility's metering or regulating equipment. The utility shall document the specific basis for the discontinuance and, where practicable, leave written notice at the premises stating the reason.

(c) A utility may not discontinue residential service for nonpayment where the customer has delivered, before the discontinuance date stated in the notice, a certificate from a licensed physician or public health official stating that discontinuance would be a serious and immediate threat to the health or safety of a person residing at the premises. The certificate postpones discontinuance for ten (10) days. The postponement shall be continued for one (1) additional ten (10) day period upon delivery of an additional certificate. The utility shall also offer a reasonable payment arrangement to any customer who demonstrates financial hardship.

(d) A utility may not discontinue residential service for nonpayment (1) before 8:00 a.m. or after 3:00 p.m. prevailing local time; (2) on a day, or on the day preceding a day, on which the utility's business office is not open to the public; or (3) after noon on the day preceding a day on which the office is closed. This subsection does not apply to discontinuance under subsection (b).

(e) Except as provided in subsection (b), a utility shall not discontinue residential service for nonpayment unless it has mailed or personally delivered written notice to the customer at least fourteen (14) days before the proposed discontinuance date. The notice must state: (1) the amount past due; (2) the date on or after which service will be discontinued unless payment or an arrangement is made; (3) the telephone number and address at which the customer may arrange payment or dispute the bill; (4) the availability of the medical certificate postponement; (5) the customer's right to file an informal complaint with the commission's consumer affairs division; and (6) the information required by 170 IAC 4-1-16.6 regarding energy assistance during the winter period.

(f) A utility shall not discontinue service for nonpayment of charges that are the subject of an unresolved dispute filed under 170 IAC 16-1 where the customer is paying the undisputed portion of the bill.

(g) Where service has been discontinued, the utility shall reconnect service within one (1) working day after the customer has paid the past-due amount, made an acceptable payment arrangement, or otherwise remedied the cause of discontinuance, and shall not impose a reconnection charge that exceeds the charge on file in its approved tariff.

(Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission; 170 IAC 4-1-16; filed Mar 3, 2008, 3:20 p.m.: 31 IR 1722)

heading: Home energy assistance; disconnection to recipients
body_text:
170 IAC 4-1-16.6 Home energy assistance; disconnection to recipients

(a) A utility shall not discontinue residential electric service for nonpayment during the period December 1 through March 15 to a customer who is receiving, or who has applied for and is eligible to receive, assistance under IC 4-4-33.

(b) The utility shall accept as proof of eligibility either the award letter issued by the Indiana Housing and Community Development Authority or its designee, or written notification from that agency that an application is pending.

(c) Within five (5) days after receiving a notice under subsection (b), the utility shall record the protection in its customer information system and shall suspend any pending discontinuance order for that customer.

(d) Nothing in this section relieves a customer of liability for service furnished. Amounts past due remain subject to a payment arrangement under 170 IAC 4-1-16(c).

(Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission; 170 IAC 4-1-16.6; filed Mar 3, 2008, 3:20 p.m.: 31 IR 1722)

heading: Informal complaints; review
body_text:
(a) A customer who is dissatisfied with the utility's response to an informal complaint may request that the commission's consumer affairs division review the matter.

(b) The utility shall respond to a consumer affairs inquiry within ten (10) days, and shall provide the account history, the notices issued, and a statement of its position.

(c) The division shall issue a written determination, and the utility shall comply with that determination or file a formal complaint under 170 IAC 1-1.1.

(Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission; 170 IAC 16-1-4; filed Mar 3, 2008, 3:20 p.m.: 31 IR 1722)

heading: Informal complaints; customer rights during review
body_text:
(a) While an informal complaint is under review by the consumer affairs division, the utility shall not discontinue service for the disputed charges if the customer pays the undisputed portion of the bill.

(b) The utility shall tell the customer, in writing, of the customer's right to file an informal complaint, at the time it denies a dispute.

(c) The review period ends on the date the division mails its written determination to the customer and the utility.

(Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission; 170 IAC 16-1-5; filed Mar 3, 2008, 3:20 p.m.: 31 IR 1722; readopted filed Dec 12, 2024, 2:05 p.m.: 20241218-IR-170240455RFA)

heading: Informal complaints; disconnection hold
body_text:
(a) A utility shall not discontinue service for the disputed amount while a complaint is under review by the consumer affairs division or the commission, and not sooner than ten (10) days after the division or commission issues its decision.

(b) A customer who files a complaint shall notify the utility of the complaint reference number, and the utility shall record it in its customer information system.

(c) The utility shall report complaint outcomes to the commission as required by IC 8-1-1-3(a).

(Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission; 170 IAC 16-1-7; filed Mar 3, 2008, 3:20 p.m.: 31 IR 1722)

heading: FESOP; limitations on operation of engines
body_text:
(a) This section applies to a stationary reciprocating internal combustion engine used as an emergency or standby generator at a source that is subject to this rule.

(b) The owner or operator shall limit operation for maintenance checks and readiness testing to one hundred (100) hours per calendar year.

(c) The owner or operator shall keep a log of the date, duration, and purpose of each operation and shall retain the log for five (5) years.

heading: Emission limits for nitrogen oxides; turbines
body_text:
(a) This section establishes the nitrogen oxides emission standard for new stationary combustion turbines that commence construction after the applicability date in the subpart.

(b) The owner or operator of a turbine firing natural gas shall not discharge into the atmosphere any gases that contain nitrogen oxides in excess of 15 ppm at 15 percent oxygen.

(c) Compliance is determined by a performance test conducted in accordance with the methods referenced in this subpart.
